election_dates.primarySnippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.007(a): The general primary election date is the first Tuesday in March in each even-numbered year.
election_dates.generalSnippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.002: The general election for state and county officers shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even-numbered years.

state_background_check.value: No — Texas's felony-disqualification requirement (Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001(a)(4)) applies only to "a public elective office in this state" by its own text, not federal office; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001: "(a) To be eligible to be a candidate for, or elected or appointed to, a public elective office in this state, a person must: ... (4) have not been finally convicted of a felony from which the person has not been pardoned or otherwise released from the resulting disabilities..." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

employment_record.value: Tennessee Titans linebacker (2006-2010); Dallas-Fort Worth Regional Director of Voter Protection for Battleground Texas (after graduating law school 2014); special assistant in the Department of Housing and Urban Development's Office of General Counsel (2016); civil rights attorney at Perkins Coie law firm
employment_record.snippet: In four seasons for the Titans between 2007 and 2010, Allred appeared in 32 games and recorded 46 tackles. [ 18 ] On October 10, 2010, [ 19 ] during a Titans game with the Dallas Cowboys , he was severely injured in the neck during a game when he collided with Cowboys player Martellus Bennett . [ 20 ] He subsequently decided to retire from football and go to law school, [ 20 ] and he became a free agent before the 2011 season without signing with another team. [ 21 ] Law [ edit ] Allred with Secretary Castro in 2016 In 2011, Allred enrolled at the UC Berkeley School of Law . He worked as a research assistant for professor and author Ian Haney López and graduated in 2014 with a Juris Doctor degree. [ 22 ] [ 14 ] After graduating from law school, Allred worked for Battleground Texas as its Dallas-Fort Worth Regional Director of Voter Protection, overseeing the state's first coordinated voter protection program. His responsibilities included overseeing the voter registration efforts of volunteers and managing a poll watcher program. In 2016, he worked as a special assistant in the Department of Housing and Urban Development 's Office of General Counsel alongside then-Secretary Julian Castro in the Obama administration. [ 23 ] Subsequently, Allred worked as a civil rights attorney [ 2 ] at the law firm Perkins Coie , where he was a voting rights litigator and counsel to clients including national and state political candidates and advocacy organizations.

platform.value: Opposes current immigration enforcement as designed to generate fear and profit private detention corporations; supports abolishing ICE and redistributing its functions to accountable agencies, prosecuting bad actors and profiteering corporations, guaranteeing due process and legal representation, and a path to citizenship for people already part of American communities.
platform.snippet:
What Trump has built is not immigration enforcement. It is a system designed to generate fear and funnel money to
corporations that profit from locking people up. It does not reduce illegal immigration. It creates chaos. And it makes
us less safe.
ENFORCEMENT: Abolish ICE and redistribute its functions to agencies bound by real standards and accountability.
ACCOUNTABILITY: Expose and prosecute bad actors who have broken the law and corporations profiteering from
this inhumane regime.
DUE PROCESS: Every person on American soil deserves their day in court with real legal representation.
REFORM: Millions of people already part of our communities deserve a real path to citizenship.
THE BORDER: Order and humanity are not opposites. A well-funded, well-staffed legal system is the real answer.
Colin Allred's immigration agenda starts with honesty: the current system is broken by design, the bad
actors must be held accountable, and we owe it to this country to build something better. Less cruelty. More
order. An America that finally lives up to its promise.

platform.value: Blames tariffs and price gouging for rising grocery costs, opposes cuts to renewable energy he says raise utility bills, criticizes pharmaceutical pricing, and cites high childcare costs and fixed-income seniors being left behind; his "A More Affordable Texas Agenda" calls for ending price gouging and repealing policies he says drive up costs.
platform.snippet:
Groceries: Tariffs and price gouging raise the cost of basics.
Utilities: Trump's cuts to renewables stick Texans with higher power bills.
Healthcare: Big Pharma charges families three times more than other countries.
Childcare: Families spend more than their rent just to give kids a safe place to learn and grow.
Seniors: Retirees on fixed incomes are left behind as costs rise.
Colin Allred's A More Affordable Texas Agenda is simple: end the price gouging, repeal the
bad policies, and put Texans first. That means lower costs, more opportunity, and a
government that finally works for working families again.

platform.value: Attributes high health care, tariff, and tax costs to corporate lobbying influence; proposed a 12-point Anti-Corruption Plan targeting drug pricing influence, tariff exemptions for donors, and tax loopholes, with further reforms planned for the courts and executive branch.
platform.snippet:
Corruption isn't abstract — it shows up in Texans' bills every month.
Health care: Big Pharma keeps drug prices high by buying influence.
Tariffs: Big donors get tariff exemptions while household bills rise beyond control.
Taxes: Lobbyists carve loopholes that leave working families paying more.
Colin Allred's plan is simple: stop corruption, lower costs, and make government work
for Texans — not for the powerful few. This 12-point Anti-Corruption Plan is a strong
foundation — practical reforms we can act on now to start unrigging the system. And it's only
the beginning. Colin also knows that we need additional reforms to take on corruption in the
courts, the executive branch, and every place where special interests tilt the playing field
against Texans.

bio_summary.value: Colin Zachary Allred (born April 15, 1983) is an American politician, civil rights lawyer, and former professional football player who served as the U.S. representative for Texas's 32nd congressional district from 2019 to 2025. The district included the northeastern corner of Dallas as well as many of its northeastern suburbs. He is a member of the Democratic Party , and is its nominee for the 33rd congressional district in 2026. Before entering politics, Allred was a linebacker who played for the Tennessee Titans of the National Football League (NFL) for four seasons. After being released, he left football to pursue a degree in law. Allred received his J.D. from the University of California, Berkeley . He then held multiple positions in the Obama administration , first at the Department of Housing and Urban Development and later at the Executive Office for United States Attorneys .
